title: Geofence rules
summary: The v1 engine: one fixed chain per device and geofence. The top row is how a rule comes to run. The middle row turns a committed reading into a location fix, a condition and rule state. Membership changes and sustained absence leave as two kinds of transition, which Laravel projects into geofence events and alert episodes.

boxes.label: Location binding
boxes.detail: Says which parameters of a device's applied configuration are its latitude and longitude, and optionally accuracy, with a maximum age, a future-skew limit and whether unknown accuracy is allowed. It names the configuration and generation and has its own revision.

boxes.label: Geofence saved
boxes.detail: Saving a polygon with its assigned devices creates one activation batch. For each device Laravel builds the four-node chain (location source, membership, sustained condition, alert), has the runtime compile it and requests a deployment. Removed devices get a disable. An item that fails is marked and can be retried; the others go ahead.

boxes.label: Rule execution
boxes.detail: The runtime checks the binding against the device it stores: same configuration and applied generation, no review required, coordinates mapped from source metrics in degrees. A new execution starts with condition unknown and no episode. If the device's applied configuration changes later, or the device needs review, the rule is suspended with binding_changed.

boxes.label: Committed telemetry
boxes.detail: Rules and DAGs share one consumer and one checkpoint. A rule sees the events of its bound device only, and never readings received or observed before it was activated.

boxes.label: Resolve a location fix
boxes.detail: Latitude and longitude must be in the same event with equal observed and received times, good quality, numeric, in degrees and in range, and timestamped by the source. Values from different events are never combined. A fix is live-eligible only if it is not historical and is younger than the binding's maximum age.

boxes.label: Unknown fix
boxes.detail: Reasons include incomplete_fix, incoherent_fix, invalid_quality, untrusted_time, future_time, accuracy_required and stale_fix. The rule's condition becomes unknown and pending evidence is dropped. Unknown never clears an active episode. Historical, duplicate and out-of-order fixes are ignored without changing anything.

boxes.label: Classify against polygon
boxes.detail: The polygon is one closed simple ring of 3 to 256 vertices, projected locally. The uncertainty band is the larger of the rule's buffer and the fix's reported accuracy; a point within the band of the boundary is unknown.

boxes.label: Rule state
boxes.detail: Stored per execution and updated in the same transaction as the checkpoint. Outside evidence counts samples since the first outside fix; a gap longer than max_gap_seconds or evidence past its expiry resets it. When the consumer is idle a timer tick re-evaluates every rule, so staleness and a due duration are noticed without new telemetry.

boxes.label: entered / exited
boxes.detail: Emitted when the condition goes straight from inside to outside (exited) or from outside to inside (entered). A change through unknown emits nothing. The transition's ID is a hash of the definition, the event and the kind, so it is stored once.

boxes.label: activated / cleared
boxes.detail: Activated: outside for at least outside_for_seconds with at least minimum_samples fixes and evidence still fresh; it starts a new episode. Cleared: an active episode and a fix inside. Each is identified by definition, episode and kind.

boxes.label: Alert episode
boxes.detail: Laravel accepts a transition only if it matches the active deployment's rule, version, device and definition hash, and stores it once. Activated opens the alert for that deployment and episode; cleared closes it.

boxes.label: Geofence event journal
boxes.detail: For a workflow that belongs to a geofence assignment, each transition becomes one geofence event and one integration event: geofence.entered.v1, geofence.exited.v1, geofence.wandering_started.v1 or geofence.wandering_resolved.v1.

steps.text: A device with a location binding is assigned to a geofence, with a policy: how long outside, how many fixes, the largest gap and an uncertainty buffer.
Laravel builds the fixed v1 chain for that device, the runtime compiles it, and it is deployed as workflow.deploy.v1.
The runtime checks the binding against the device it stores and starts the rule with condition unknown.
Each committed event from the device is resolved into a location fix from that one event.
If the coordinates are missing, mismatched, bad quality, not timestamped by the source or too old, the fix is unknown and pending evidence is dropped.
A live fix is classified against the polygon. A point within the uncertainty band of the boundary is unknown.
The condition updates the rule's stored state: outside counts as evidence, inside resets it.
Going straight from inside to outside, or back, emits exited or entered.
Outside for long enough with enough fixes emits activated; seen inside again during an episode emits cleared.
Laravel checks the transition against the deployment and opens or clears the alert episode.
Entered and exited are journaled as geofence events and integration events.
Activated and cleared are journaled too, as wandering started and wandering resolved.
